go2|measured.label: Go2 camera, 0.37 m · measured detector and matcher

raised|measured.label: Raised camera, 1.0 m · measured detector and matcher

caveat: One household in one home, 248 searches a month, each policy run from five different starting positions and pooled: the robot starts each search where the last one ended, so the whole month depends on where it began, and the lowest and highest per-start values are shown beside the pooled one. Differences of a few points are noise. Two towels that never leave the bathroom are 106 of the 248 questions and most of what is findable at 0.37 m, so the 'towels' and 'other things' columns matter more than the overall one. 'Measured detector and matcher' replays what OWLv2 and DINOv2 did on these pictures: a thing is detected with the recall measured for its kind (scaled by its size), and named right with the accuracy measured between this household's own two things of that kind, otherwise named as the other; the draw is fixed per picture, so every policy meets the same misses and mistakes. False alarms on untracked objects are not replayed. The oracle goes straight to the nearest position that truly shows the thing, or answers 'cannot be found'. Words in brackets name the fallback when the thing has never been seen: 'nearest' goes to the nearest place not yet looked at, 'kind' first to places where things of the same kind were seen, 'rooms' first to a whole-room look at a room not yet looked in. Running out of looks counts as wrong even when nothing could have been found; only an explicit 'cannot be found' counts as right then, and only the chance-over-cost rule ever gives one. Two audits of this benchmark are on the Audits page; the second's findings are fixed in these numbers, which have not themselves been re-audited.
